data.title: Dogecoin down by 44%, hits 2026’s lowest price — More downside ahead?
data.description:
Dogecoin [DOGE] has been more bark than bite lately.

Last week’s sell-off pushed it down to a new yearly low on the charts and unfortunately, it doesn’t look like it’ll get back up anytime soon.

A yearly low with an oversold RSI

At the time of writing, Dogecoin was valued at $0.058. This followed a 3.3% dip over the day.

Things really fell apart on 14th November. DOGE fell from $0.065 to $0.057 in a single day. It also briefly hit $0.055, the lowest level of 2026. DOGE’s volume jumped too, implying that too many were selling at once.

Now, while it managed a small bounce to about $0.060 later, it wasn’t able to hold on to that level.

For context, DOGE was above $0.10 in late September. That’s 44% gone… in less than two months.

The RSI was at 28.9, hinting at oversold conditions. It even sank close to 18 during the crash. The MACD was still deep in the red, though the bars were shrinking just a tad.

Simply put, while the sellers seemed to be worn out, buyers are yet to show up.

Futures traders are gone, and ETFs are quiet

Finally, leverage has been draining out too, with Open Interest sliding from about $475 million on the 11th to $362.5 at press time.

That’s a quarter of it gone in a week!

It is a nervous state of things, and one look at the funding rates will tell you why. It was red during the crash of the 14th, flipped a couple more times, and at press time was back to 0.0052%.

Some traders may be betting on a bounce again, but not in big numbers. Not yet.

ETFs have been even quieter. According to data from SoSoValue, Spot DOGE ETFs haven’t seen a single day of inflows or outflows since mid-October. A whole month of nothing.

Their total net assets still dropped though. We went from $17 million in late September to about $9.74 million at the time of writing. In simple words, Dogecoin’s falling price has been shrinking what’s already there.

Final Summary

  • Dogecoin fell to a 2026 low, and its RSI fell to an oversold territory.
  • Spot ETFs have seen no flows since mid-October.

data.title: How did Coinbase stop deepfake Elon Musk’s promise to double your crypto?
data.description:
Scammers recently used a fake video of Elon Musk to get people to send them crypto. It didn’t go to plan.

Especially since according to Coinbase, it blocked a big chunk of those transfers before the money could disappear.

A fake Musk livestream drew 500K viewers…

… and Coinbase stopped $4.7 million from reaching scammers.

Someone put out a YouTube livestream made to look like a Tesla flying car demo. On screen was an AI-made Elon Musk, and the pitch was to send crypto and get 2x back.

More than half a million people tuned in. The stream flashed wallet addresses and QR codes. So, sending money took just a scan.

In a blog post, Coinbase laid out what happened. In about two hours, hundreds of its users tried to send funds to the scammers. Its automated fraud system caught about 91% of that.

The real Musk had nothing to do with any of it.

Here, it’s worth pointing out that Coinbase hasn’t said how much of the remaining 9% actually got through.

Coinbase fought AI with AI

data.title: Binance launches 7 bStocks pairs and Anthropic token sale – Details
data.description:
On the 18th of November, Binance opened seven new tokenized-stock (bStocks) trading pairs, alongside launching a high-stakes Anthropic token sale. However, under the surface, on-chain trackers watched as Binance-linked hackers pushed millions through THORChain.

What is the bStocks expansion?

In its latest announcement, Binance revealed that it had added Spot/Convert pairs for seven tokenized securities. They are EWJB, EWTB, EWZB, EWZSB, IWMB, MELIB, and NUB, all of which are paired with USDT.

The announcement also reported that,

Rebalancing Bots services will be enabled within 24 hours of it being listed on Spot.

Also, maker fees will be zero until the 30th of November.

However, there are a few disclaimers attached to this announcement as well. First, bStocks are simply certificates, not shares. They are also not available to citizens of the U.S., and grant the holder no ownership in the underlying company.

Binance’s Anthropic sale: All about ANTx

Meanwhile, Binance Wallet’s Anthropic IPO xStocks Campaign ran from 06:00 to 14:00 UTC on the 18th of November, with a 100 USDC minimum and a 500 million USDC cap.

The displayed 70–78 USDC per token is indicative only, excluding fees, and implies an Anthropic valuation of roughly $1.26 trillion to $1.41 trillion. And the final price will be set after the sales window closes, based on demand, valuation, and issuance arrangements.

However, there is a massive catch. A 5% xStocks partner service fee lifts break-even to roughly 73.50–81.90 USDC, so as a result, a 10% token move will only net about 4.8%.

Moreover, allocation is non-guaranteed – users may receive full, partial, or zero allocation, with unused funds auto-refunded.

Finally, ANTx carries no voting, dividend, or ownership rights. Binance itself claims no ownership rights of the token.

An on-chain reality check

In a separate report on the 18th of November, Lookonchain reported that Binance hackers split 74,880 Ethereum [ETH], worth nearly $137M, into seven addresses. After this, they routed 7,598 ETH, or nearly $13.7M in tokens, through THORChain to six new Bitcoin [BTC] addresses.

If the full amount is laundered, the fees of this transaction will run up to $137K–$684K. RUNE rose 6.1% to $0.5504 on the news at press time.

Binance – Hollow inside?

Binance’s bStocks rollout and the ANTx sale show genuine demand for on-chain stock exposure, but they also show how much of the risk sits with the user, with fees baked into the entry price, no shareholder rights, and backing that the platform itself won’t verify.

Add the THORChain laundering trail, and the picture is clear – despite Binance’s positive moves, the shadows of its past hacks still loom. For now, until the final ANTx pricing lands and bStocks volume proves itself, the smart move is to price the risk before pricing the upside.

Final Summary

  • Binance expanded its reach into the tokenized equities market. Interestingly, on the same day, its Anthropic ANTx sale drew commitments of 100 to 500,000 USDC per wallet.
  • Meanwhile, Lookonchain reported that Binance-linked hackers split 74,880 ETH into seven addresses and routed 7,598 ETH through THORChain to six new Bitcoin addresses, with estimated laundering fees of $137K–$684K.

data.title: Ethena USDe supply on Avalanche crosses $100M – Yet ENA bears tighten grip below THIS
data.description:
The USDe supply on Avalanche has crossed $100 million, the Ethena [ENA] Ecosystem social media handle announced on X.

Increased adoption and ecosystem integration via EthenaPay on the Avalanche blockchain drove the synthetic dollar growth.

The USDe supply was just $20 million towards the end of October. Ethena has been building toward this Avalanche push for months, according to reports.

Ethena Pay, the self-custody mobile and money payments app, can automatically earn daily yield, tiered cashback in AVAX based on monthly spending, and allows free, instant transfers to other Ethena Pay users.

These features helped explain the USDe growth, but they might not contribute much to ENA token price growth.

Whale deposits highlight short-term ENA loss-making

Popular onchain tracking platform Lookonchain posted that a whale had deposited 20 million ENA tokens, worth $2.33 million, onto Binance within the past 24 hours.

This whale had bought 37.96 million ENA, worth $10.29 million at around $0.27 a month ago.

Deposits onto exchanges are not proof of selling, but they do highlight increased available supply ready to be sold. It can be taken as a sign of partial capitulation of the whale’s initial position, following ENA’s steady downtrend over the past month.

The ENA 1-day chart has flipped from bullish to bearish in its swing structure. The past month’s steady selling drove a price move below $0.1348, the previous swing low.

The descending trendline resistance was unbroken. To add to the bearish pressure, the former local support zone at $0.18 had also been decisively breached. This helped accelerate the selling pressure on ENA that led to the bearish trend shift.

Short-term ENA outlook- Consolidation phase underway

On the 1-hour timeframe, ENA was trading within a range that reached from $0.110 to $0.122. The technical indicators on this timeframe were neutral, further highlighting the short-term consolidation type price action.

In the coming days, a move past the range high would likely result in a bounce to $0.131. This level was a higher timeframe supply zone, and ENA might struggle to climb any further.

Final Summary

  • The USDe supply growth was powered by increased adoption and the Ethena Pay app’s utility.
  • The ENA token was trending bearishly alongside the wider crypto market, and has settled into a short-term range.

data.title: Top 7 cloud mining platforms of November 2026
data.description:
Cloud mining allows users to mine cryptocurrencies by renting computing power. They can mine crypto without buying or owning any equipment or worrying about its maintenance. Mining is an essential part of the cryptocurrency space, and with cloud mining, the space is opened up for people with little to no technical knowledge.

Cloud mining provides an alternative to anyone in the crypto space who wants to participate in Bitcoin mining without buying any expensive mining equipment or managing hardware. Here is our list of the top 7 cloud mining platforms of the month:

1. NiceHash

NiceHash has a marketplace that provides an alternative to conventional cloud mining contracts instead of functioning as a fixed-term mining provider. Instead of functioning as a fixed-term mining provider, it connects hashrate buyers and sellers through a marketplace.

For users who want to understand mining costs and rewards and monitor prices, it is a great option. The platform also supports proof-of-work algorithms and lets users mine Bitcoin and other PoW assets through pools of their choice, where payouts are settled in BTC.

2. KuMining

KuMining is associated with the KuCoin ecosystem and gives users a chance to explore cryptocurrency mining contracts without having their own mining machines. Users can compare various available mining contracts in terms of hashrate pricing, mining durations, and choose the right one depending on their requirements.

Since KuCoin is an established exchange ecosystem, KuMining gained a lot of attention through it. Users who understand exchange-based accounts and digital asset transactions can find the platform to be useful. It is a good option for existing crypto traders who want to use mining services related to an exchange.

3. ViaBTC

ViaBTC is popular and known for its mining pool services and lets users connect their mining equipment to a shared mining pool and take part in cryptocurrency reward distribution. Most of the platform’s services are for users who are already part of mining hardware operations and want to establish a pool rather than attempting to mine on their own.

Multiple cryptocurrencies and mining-related tools on the platform allow users to monitor account balances, payout information, and mining performance. ViaBTC can be great for anyone who wants to research professional mining operations and alternative mining pool services.

4. Hashing24

Hashing24 is for users who want to focus on accessing mining capacity through contract-based arrangements. For anyone wanting to be a part of cloud mining without buying ASIC hardware or managing it.

It has been a part of the cryptocurrency space since 2012 and focuses primarily on Bitcoin mining. Users can buy mining power that is measured in terahashes, with contracts running over different periods of time depending on the plan.

5. BeMine

BeMine has fractional ownership of ASIC mining hardware rather than relying on renting traditional cloud mining contracts. The mining company is based on the principles of security and transparency. Mining can be done without the owner’s direct participation.

Users can also buy 1/100 of a share of any specific ASIC, which can be a viable option for anyone who wants to start mining without buying an expensive machine entirely.

6. BitFuFu

BitFuFu is another popular option for users, and it operates in the Bitcoin mining infrastructure sector and offers options for miner sales, mining equipment hosting, and cloud mining. The platform aims to empower the global Bitcoin network and offers a one-stop solution for a cheap and easy way to earn Bitcoin.

There is an online interface that lets users monitor mining-related information and account activity, making it easy and convenient for those who are new to the space.

7. Bitdeer

Bitdeer provides cloud hashrate services, infrastructure services, and mining hardware solutions for a wide range of users. The cloud mining products let users buy computing power without buying or maintaining any mining machines. They can also choose the hashrate capacities and mining durations that suit their requirements well.

The company is also involved in large-scale mining infrastructure and operates mining facilities and provides services connected to cryptocurrency mining hardware.

Final conclusion

Cloud mining is an alternative and interesting way for users to become a part of the cryptocurrency space. While the crypto mining space may look daunting for a lot of people, cloud mining provides an easy segue into it.

Every platform mentioned on this list has its own advantages; however, it is advised to do your own research before investing.

Disclaimer. Readers are encouraged to do their own research. Ambcrypto is not liable for any outcomes related to the use of information, products, or services mentioned. This content may include affiliate or partner links.

data.title: Render outpaces Bitcoin and Ethereum – But its rebound can gather steam ONLY IF…
data.description:
Render [RENDER] was among the top gainers for the day in the crypto market. The native token of the decentralized GPU-based rendering solution provider network has rallied 4% for the day, comfortably surpassing the gains of the leaders, Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH], at 0.06% and 0.49%, respectively, at the time of writing.

Alongside its price move, the Open Interest was up by 9.15% for the day. A high OI uptick alongside a price bounce generally points to speculative buying and short-term bullish belief.

The spot CVD was also slowly climbing higher, while the funding rates remained close to zero, according to Coinalyze data. This meant that spot buying was beginning to recover, and the threat of a long squeeze on the back of the swift OI uptick was minimal.

In other news, Render participated in Solana’s Breakpoint 2026, showcasing its immersive digital art exhibition.

RENDER long-term consolidation not yet shaken off

Since December 2025, RENDER bulls have stubbornly defended the $1.24 support zone. Marked as the lows of a long-term range, the weekly chart above highlighted the lack of a decisive trend.

The OBV has been moving sideways since May and has not managed to set notable new highs or lows. The Awesome Oscillator also meandered about the zero line, unlike October-November of 2025 when bearish momentum was dominant.

The $1.24 support, range high of $2.60, and the mid-range level at $1.92 (close to the $2.0 supply zone) were worth investor scrutiny for price trend clues.

Retest of former local floor colors short-term RENDER outlook

The 4-hour chart was more encouraging for traders as there was a noticeable price trend. The OBV had slipped considerably earlier this month, a result of the market-wide sell-off towards the end of the previous week.

The $1.45-$1.50 former support zone has now been retested as a supply zone. It is likely that RENDER would continue its H4 downtrend and seek the $1.31 lows next.

Final Summary

  • The Render short-term speculative belief appeared to be bullish following Tuesday’s 11.56% price rally.
  • The 4-hour chart highlighted why bears were likely in control of the market, while the weekly chart illuminated a long-term range formation.

data.title: What is Ethereum actually for? A judge and Vitalik Buterin both left it open
data.description:
the 16th of November, a federal judge acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno in the “first of its kind” wire fraud prosecution over a $25 million Ethereum exploit. This judgement came about after the government failed to prove the brothers made any “material misrepresentation.”

The ruling, filed in the Southern District of New York (24-CR-293), came the same day as when Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley pitched stablecoins as a backup for banks.

On a similar note, Ethereum [ETH] co-founder Vitalik Buterin argued that digital assets do not match up to investing in houses. These three developments, when taken together, compound the question of what crypto is actually for.

What was the case about?

On the 2nd of April 2023, the brothers seemingly exploited a bug in the MEV-Boost relay software, due to which they could view transactions that sandwich traders believed were private.

The brothers’ alleged proposal for replacement transactions, in turn, resulted in massive losses of roughly $25 million within seconds.

The government called the prosecution,

The very first of its kind.

Finally, on the 16th of November 2026, Judge Jessica G. L. Clarke, when granting an acquittal, wrote,

The question before the Court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos’ conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes.

She continued,

It is simply whether the evidence at trial, construed in a light most favorable to the Government, could support wire fraud and related convictions in this case. Because the Government failed to prove that the Peraire-Buenos made any material misrepresentations in the execution of their scheme, the motion is granted.

The court analyzed the government’s theories – including the “lure transactions” and the so-called “false signature,” and found nothing that could support a wire fraud conviction.

What are crypto’s varying use cases?

A couple of days later, on the 18th of November, Horsley posted on X:

Rolling bank outages in the AI era – Consider having some stablecoins or crypto just in case.

The post came as thousands of Chase, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo customers reported being unable to access their accounts.

Vitalik Buterin, in a separate post on November 18, argued that younger generations have been investing in digital assets over real estate options; doing so, he noted, reduces –

Perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive.

But he added a condition: housing had the advantage of being –

A culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can’t easily liquidate.

He also wrote,

Modern platforms encourage the opposite of this, leading to more irresponsible behavior… We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets.

Is crypto unequivalent to TradFi?

The three developments have been framing crypto’s developing role separately, but these assets have a long way to go before they can fully replace TradFi.

Vitalik Buterin himself leaves the question open, as he observed,

We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets.

The ruling did not answer that question, nor did the outage.

Final Summary

  • A federal judge acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno in a “first of its kind” wire fraud case over a $25M Ethereum exploit, finding that there was no material misrepresentation.
  • The same day, Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley urged users to hold stablecoins amid major U.S. bank outages, and Vitalik Buterin said digital assets still lack housing’s “safe, non-crazy” default properties.

data.title: Dumping to stacking in just three months? What’s going on with XRP whales?
data.description:
XRP’s price dipped under $1, and most of the market looks ready to walk away. Not the whales, though. At least not yet.

Is that enough to stop the fall?

Whales are pulling their stash off Binance!

According to recent data, XRP whales have taken out more than $127 million in XRP off Binance since 10th November. Net outflows went between $12-$33 million over the past week, including about $21 million on the 16th alone!

Not too long ago, it was the other way around.

In August, XRP went up by about 72% and back above $1.50. Whales were dumping as much as $75 million on Binance in a single day!

If you look further back, you’ll see that XRP hit $3.55 in the summer of 2025. In that time, some days saw more than $100 million flood in.

One day even hit close to $270 million.

When coins leave an exchange, people usually want to hold. However, don’t get excited yet. Some of this might just be Binance moving its money around.

Remember when it was topping up its reserves after the October hack?

Lowest weekly close in two years…

data.title: Solana Foundation takes ‘majority interest’ in CoinGecko – What changes next?
data.description:
The Solana Foundation now holds a “majority interest” in CoinGecko, its Chief Product Officer Vibhu Norby said on X.

CoinGecko described the arrangement as “backing” when it announced the news at Breakpoint in London on the 17th of November. Neither announcement gave the exact stake, price, or governance terms.

Four days earlier, CoinGecko had promoted independent ownership as a reason to choose its data service over Binance-owned CoinMarketCap. It now plans to explore trading alongside its market data.

Could users trade directly on CoinGecko?

The Foundation said it planned to bring Solana-powered trading to CoinGecko’s website, app, and GeckoTerminal. Notably, CoinGecko said it was still exploring trading features.

For Solana, that could mean reaching traders where they already look up prices. CoinGecko draws well over 50 million monthly sessions, according to the Foundation.

On the 17th of November, Solana [SOL] recorded $50.44 billion in 30-day DEX spot volume, whereas Ethereum [ETH] recorded $53.86 billion.

Norby also flagged broader coverage of stocks and real-world assets [RWAs]. AMBCrypto reported that Solana’s RWA value reached $5 billion in October.

By the 12th of November, tokenized equity supply stood at $607 million, with xStocks accounting for 75%.

Who sets CoinGecko’s data rules?

CoinGecko’s API guide warned that exchange ownership could raise questions about bias in rankings and trading volumes. AMBCrypto covered similar concerns when Binance bought CoinMarketCap in 2020.

After Norby’s disclosure, an X user called the new arrangement “a credibility problem.”

CoinGecko said its methods would stay “transparent, publicly accessible.” Readers can check how it calculates prices, but the announcements leave open who can approve changes to those rules.

Brera Holdings disclosed board rights in a separate 2025 deal involving Solmate. A later filing specified that the Foundation could nominate up to two directors, depending on board size. For CoinGecko, board seats and approval rights remain undisclosed.

Final Summary

  • The Solana Foundation, according to its product chief, Vibhu Norby. Four days earlier, CoinGecko had promoted its independent ownership.
  • They plan to add Solana-powered trading to CoinGecko. CoinGecko says the rules it uses to calculate prices will stay public.

data.title: Bitcoin tests $62K support – Can BTC bulls hold without Spot demand?
data.description:
After the $3 billion crypto liquidation wave that occurred on the 13th and 14th of November, the liquidation numbers have slowed slightly.

A relatively small liquidation number of just over $563 million was recorded on the 15th, and just $289.9 million in liquidations across the market on the 16th of November, according to CoinGlass data.

AMBCrypto reported recently that the Bitcoin [BTC] price move down to $62k acted as a leverage flush. It remains to be seen whether the bulls can enforce a recovery from here.

THIS supply cluster could keep BTC’s revival hopes alive

In a post on X, Glassnode showed that the price was trading just above a dense cluster of short-term holder supply. The darker cells denote more BTC supply in STH custody at that cost basis.

The $62k-$63k area was a particularly dense STH supply cluster, and in recent days, there has been a positive reaction. The same area had been the base of the previous impulse move higher in mid-August.

If this area is breached, it could lead to another capitulation and new lows being formed.

Sustained demand is necessary to stabilize Bitcoin price trends

Crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. noted that the bulls were trying to push BTC prices higher in the futures market. The hourly taker buy-sell imbalance reached +8,709 BTC on Monday, the 16th of November.

Yet, the price was yet to push higher. The first areas of interest were the imbalance at $66.2k-$66.9k and the local high at $70,214.

Deeply negative apparent demand (30-day sum), with a 30-day reading of -247,700 BTC and a yearly measurement of -1.21 million BTC, highlighted severe market stress.

Crypto analyst Darkfost wrote that the metric, which is an indirect on-chain proxy based on new issuance versus changes in supply inactive for over a year, does not measure net cash outflows.

Nevertheless, it has historically been a reliable indicator that helps confirm trend strength. Right now, any price rebound without apparent demand easing toward neutral or positive levels would signal weakness.

Final Summary

  • The Bitcoin price sank to $62k, a dense pocket of short-term holder supply, and has managed to bounce to $65k in the past 48 hours.
  • There is short-term futures demand, but sustained demand is lacking and continues to signal buyer weakness.
